@@identicalOkWhy: Keys that may legitimately come back byte-identical to English — a brand name, an email address, or a word many languages borrow unchanged. Everything NOT listed here and identical to English is treated as untranslated and fails the build. Keep this list short: it is an exemption from the check that catches the most common translation failure.

items.a: Daili is free to use — calendar, lists, to-dos, habits, notes, recipes and more, with no ads and no data selling. Daili Plus is optional: one yearly price for the whole family (€9.99 in the euro area; the app shows the price in your currency) gives you 30 AI actions a month and 5 GB of Daili cloud for note pictures and recordings. Every family gets 3 AI actions a month for free.

Yes. Open app.daili.app in any browser on your computer and sign in with the same account. Calendar, lists, meals, birthdays and family are all there; photos and documents stay on your phone. The web app is in English and German.

The app speaks 25 languages, fully — including the reminders it sends: English, German, French, Spanish, Italian, Dutch, Portuguese, Polish, Czech, Slovak, Swedish, Danish, Norwegian, Finnish, Turkish, Romanian, Bulgarian, Greek, Ukrainian, Indonesian, Thai, Japanese, Korean and Chinese (Simplified and Traditional).

items.q: Which phones does it run on?
items.a: iPhone and Android, from one shared family account. Everything syncs between them — and with the web app.

Yes — that's the point. Kids and teens get their own login and see their own tasks and events. Little ones without an email address get a managed profile a parent controls, which can be upgraded to a real login later. Parents are admins and can remove a profile and its data at any time.
You can read your calendar, lists and to-dos without a connection, and changes sync as soon as you're back online. Photos and documents in the vault are always offline — they live only on your phone.

items.q: Can I bring my existing calendar?
items.a: Yes. Daili shows the calendars already on your phone — Google, Outlook, iCloud and others — next to the family calendar, on your device only. You can also add the public holidays for your country.

Your calendar, lists and family data live on our servers in Germany (EU). Photos and documents in the vault never leave your phone. Note pictures and recordings stay on your phone too, unless you choose Daili cloud (part of Daili Plus), which also stores them in Germany. Details in the privacy policy.

support.intro: We're a small team and we read everything. Write to support@daili.app — questions, problems or ideas.
support.helpsIntro: If something isn't working, it helps us a lot if you include:
helps: Your phone model and whether it's iPhone or Android
What you did, what you expected, and what happened instead
A screenshot, if you have one
support.replyTime: We usually answer within a day or two.
support.deleteIntro: You can delete your Daili account and its data at any time, in two ways:
deleteWays: In the app: Settings → Profile → Delete account.
By email: write to support@daili.app from the email address of your account, with the subject “Delete my account”.
support.deleteWhat: What happens next: your account is deactivated immediately and you receive an email with a cancellation link. After a 30-day grace period, your account and the data linked to it (profile, and any events, lists, recipes and photos you created) are permanently deleted from our servers. If you change your mind within those 30 days, the link in the email restores everything. Files in the offline vault live only on your phone and are removed when the account is deleted on that device. If you have Daili Plus, cancel it in the App Store or Google Play first — deleting your account does not cancel the subscription.
